# Notion to Discord Bot

> Free, hosted Discord bot on Cloudflare Workers that posts Notion database automation events to a Discord channel as rich embeds. No sign-up and no server-side state: the whole configuration (the Discord channel ID and an optional title) is encoded in the URL that you paste into Notion.

Hosted instance: https://notion-to-discord-bot.naas.workers.dev/

## How to build the Notion webhook URL

You can construct the URL directly from a Discord channel ID; no API call or account is needed.

1. Invite the bot to the Discord server (one time per server): https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=1314524073170042962&permissions=2048&integration_type=0&scope=bot
   For a private channel, also give the bot access to that channel.
2. Get the channel ID: in Discord, enable **User Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode**, then right-click the channel and choose **Copy Channel ID**. It is a 17–19 digit number.
3. Build the URL:
   `https://notion-to-discord-bot.naas.workers.dev/{DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID}`
4. Optional: add an embed title as the `title` query parameter, URL-encoded:
   `https://notion-to-discord-bot.naas.workers.dev/{DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID}?title=Task%20Updates`
5. In Notion, open the database → **Settings → Automations → New automation**, choose a trigger (e.g. "Page added" or "Property edited"), add the action **Send webhook**, and paste the URL. No custom headers are needed.

Example:

- Channel ID: `123456789012345678`
- Notion webhook URL: `https://notion-to-discord-bot.naas.workers.dev/123456789012345678?title=New%20Tasks`

Notes:

- The URL contains no secret, but anyone who has it can make the bot post to that channel, so don't publish it.
- Opening the generated URL in a browser shows a settings page pre-filled with its values, where the channel and title can be edited.

## What gets posted

Each Notion event becomes one Discord embed with the page's properties as fields and an "Open in Notion" link button. Supported property types include title, rich text, number, select, multi-select, status, date, people, files, checkbox, URL, email, phone, formula, relation, rollup, created/last edited time and by, unique ID, verification, place, and button.

## Endpoint

- `POST /{DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID}?title={OPTIONAL_TITLE}`: receives the JSON body of a Notion "Send webhook" automation action and posts it to the Discord channel.
- `GET /{DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID}?title={OPTIONAL_TITLE}`: the settings / URL generator page.

## Links

- [URL generator](https://notion-to-discord-bot.naas.workers.dev/): enter a channel ID, get the Notion webhook URL
- [Source code and README](https://github.com/nakanoasaservice/notion-to-discord-bot): MIT licensed; can be self-hosted on Cloudflare Workers with your own bot token
- [Notion: Database automations](https://www.notion.com/help/database-automations): how to add a "Send webhook" action
- [Discord: Where can I find my User/Server/Message ID?](https://support.discord.com/hc/en-us/articles/206346498): how to copy a channel ID

## Optional

- [Notion to Discord Relay](https://notion-to-discord-relay.naas.workers.dev/): sister project that posts through a Discord channel webhook instead of a bot, so no bot needs to be added to the server
